newsitem.title: UK: De La Rue profits fall on low banknote prices.
newsitem.headline: De La Rue profits fall on low banknote prices.

text.p: British printing and security products group De La Rue Plc said Tuesday its first-half profits results fell sharply as banknote prices slumped.

Pretax profits slid to 60.3 million pounds ($100 million) for the half from 69.1 million ($115.7 million) in the year-ago period. But results were higher than estimates, which ranged from 55 to 61 million pounds ($92.1-102.2 million).
De La Rue also raised its dividend to 7.5 pence (12.6 cents) per share from 7.25 (12.1 cents) in the year-ago period.
"There are no surprises. Although there's a reduction in profits, we are at the top end of forecasts," chief executive Jeremy Marshall said in an interview.
The company's shares rose 2.5 pence (4.1 cents) to 557.5 pence ($9.34) by 1135 GMT after touching an intraday high of 579 pence ($9.70) earlier.
On Monday, the stock scraped 542 pence ($9.01), its lowest level since September 1992 as investors nervously awaited the results, which the company had warned would be down from last year.
Marshall said banknote prices appeared to have stabilised further since June.
At that time, the firm cautioned that difficult trading conditions in its cash systems division and low banknote prices would hit its first-half results.
"We do have clear signs that the average prices we are obtaining are stabilising," Marshall said.
"Up until June, we did see some deterioration in margins because prices were going up, mainly because we're putting additional security features into notes," he added.
Banknote volumes increased by 14.5 percent in the first half ended Sept. 30, compared to the year-ago period.
"We are meeting competition on the banknote side. But the group (De La Rue) on the whole is making margins of 12 percent," Marshall said.
